exchanges.system_prompt:
You split one step of a HoldSpeak Program into smaller steps that a small model can build. You answer JSON only: {"say": "...", "parts": [{"title": "...", "brief": "...", "owns": ["..."]}]}.

RULES
- Cut the step into 2 to 4 parts, in the order they run: each part comes after the part before it.
- Together the parts own what the step owns, and nothing else. A part may own a file inside an owned folder.
  Each part owns at most 3 paths.
- One concern per part. Its brief is one to four sentences, under 400 words: what the change does and how
  the part is checked.
- Each part must fit in the size given below, with its brief and the files it owns.
- "say": one short line: the parts and why.

SIZE
The agent that builds each part (Claude Code) has a context of 64k tokens; a part must fit in 32k tokens with its brief and the files it owns.

exchanges.reply_text: {"brief":"In CallsWindow.tsx the status bar shows 'Line starting' based on a fixed 40-second timer rather than the actual line readiness signal. fields.title: Calls status bar: use line status instead of 40 s timer
fields.brief: In CallsWindow.tsx the status bar shows 'Line starting' based on a fixed 40-second timer rather than the actual line readiness signal. Replace the elapsed-time check with a direct read of the line status (ready vs. starting) so the label flips to 'Line ready' the moment the backend reports the line is up. Verified by the existing unit fixture status.ready.ts which asserts the ready label, and by a quick manual walk of the Calls window after a line start.

fields.brief: In ProgramsWindow.tsx the status bar unconditionally renders a 'skipped' segment even when the count is zero. Guard the segment so it is omitted when skipped === 0, matching the existing pattern used for other zero-count segments. Update test_program_window_words.py to assert the status bar text does not contain 'skipped' when the skipped count is zero, and still contains it when the count is positive.
